title: Breachless rollback and recovery playbook
author: Lena Ortiz
content:
Summary
---
This playbook describes the "breachless" rollback pattern: a set of runbook steps, automation primitives, and communication templates designed to restore service or model versions with minimal customer-visible errors and no data exposure. The approach emphasizes graceful degradation, in-flight request preservation, coordinated route-level fallbacks, and staged customer notices.

When to use this playbook
1) A newly deployed model or runtime change causes widespread correctness regressions (quality SLO drift) or high 5xx rates.
2) A configuration change (e.g., batching policy, KV cache eviction) causes latency spikes or systematic failures.
3) You need immediate mitigation that preserves in-flight inference and auditability while avoiding noisy customer-facing outages.

Goals and success criteria
- Restore global 5xx rate to <= SLO within the target restoration window (15–60 minutes depending on severity).
- No PII or secrets exposed in the mitigation steps.
- Customers receive clear, stage-appropriate notification (see templates).
- Postmortem artifacts (timeline, evidence, RCA) created within 48 hours.

Ownership and escalation
- Primary responder: on-call serving-runtime engineer (pagered).
- Secondary: SRE on-call and on-call product engineer for impacted product lines.
- Incident commander: assigned if severity >= Sev2.
- Escalation matrix: follow standard on-call escalation matrix (see related pages).

Key primitives used in breachless rollback
- Traffic mirroring (shadow): mirror production traffic to the previous stable model to validate behavior before switching live traffic.
- Canary split and progressive traffic shift: move 5/15/50/100 percent in timed intervals with health checks.
- In-flight request draining: avoid killing worker that holds KV or attention cache; allow sticky sessions to finish or be drained via drain endpoint.
- Fallback policy: per-route policy that directs degraded requests to a cheaper but compatible model variant or a cached response path.
- Circuit breaker + throttling: limit new long-running requests while preserving short/latency-sensitive calls.
- Audit logging toggle: ensure any investigative mode has audit logs enabled and retained to meet compliance.

Runbook: immediate steps (first 30 minutes)
1) Acknowledge and classify
   a) Acknowledge pager and capture initial evidence: service metrics, 5xx rates, tail latency, error traces, model version IDs.
   b) Classify impact: quality regression vs. runtime failure vs. config-induced latency.
2) Stabilize ingress
   a) If 5xx flood: enable route-level throttling to preserve core systems.
   b) If latency spike: reduce max request concurrency for affected pool and enable short-circuit cache where applicable.
3) Open a dedicated incident channel and create an incident document with this playbook attached.
4) Start shadow validation (if available)
   a) Spin up previous stable model variant in read-only shadow mode.
   b) Mirror 1–5% traffic for 10–15 minutes and compare responses (automated diff runner).
   c) If shadow shows acceptable behavior, proceed to progressive canary.
5) Progressive canary rollback
   a) Configure canary split: route 5% -> stable variant, 95% -> current. Wait 5–10 minutes and check health: error rate, latency, output-quality quick-checks.
   b) Progress to 25% -> stable for 10 minutes, then 50% if metrics are stable.
   c) If instability persists, revert to 0% and proceed to full rollback.
6) Full rollback path (if canary fails)
   a) Provision enough capacity of the stable variant (autoscale policy may be manual for older model sizes).
   b) Coordinate a timed cutover: update smart routing to prefer stable variant, preserve active connections (use connection draining windows of 30–120s).
   c) Verify observability dashboards, request traces, and end-to-end checks.
7) Communication (first notice)
   a) Send an incident acknowledgement on the incident channel and to Customer Success for impacted customers. Use the Tiered Customer Notice template below.
   b) Avoid public status update until the customer-impacting window is understood; use internal status for executive stakeholders.

Runbook: recovery and hardening (30–240 minutes)
1) Stabilize and monitor 2–4x SLO windows.
2) Collect audit logs, request samples, and top error traces. Save evidence artifacts to the incident dossier.
3) Start a scoped rollback retrospective: capture the minimal diff that caused regression.
4) Rebaseline canary tests: add lightweight QA probes that run as synthetic checks against every deployment pipeline.
5) If rollback required code changes: coordinate a follow-up deploy pipeline with an immediate-stage smoke test and extended shadowing for 1 hour.
6) Close incident with a temporary action plan: ticketed follow-ups for root cause fixes, test coverage gaps, and monitoring additions.

Customer notice templates (tiered)
- Internal short (incident channel):
"We are investigating elevated errors and latency on /v1/generate affecting a subset of customers. We are validating a rollback to the previous model variant and expect partial mitigation within 20–45 minutes. No data breach suspected. Assigned: on-call serving-runtime. Updates every 15 minutes."

- Tiered customer notice (for impacted customers via CS):
Subject: Service degradation impacting inference responses – post-mitigation update
Body:
"Hello,
We observed degraded responses from our inference system between 14:12–14:28 UTC that may have affected API calls for your tenant. We have rolled traffic back to a prior stable model variant; normal service has been restored. No customer data was exposed. Next steps: we will provide a post-incident report within 48 hours outlining root cause and remediation. If you observed specific incorrect outputs that need review, please reply to this thread and we will prioritize re-evaluation.
Regards,
Customer Success & Redwood Operations"

Status page templates (short, machine-ready)
- Public short: "We are investigating an issue affecting text generation in US region. Partial mitigation in place; customers may see degraded quality or higher latency. Status: degraded"
- Internal status payload (JSON example for automation):
{
  "incident_id": "INC-2027-1234",
  "start_time": "2027-01-10T14:12:00Z",
  "services_affected": ["inference-text-us-east"],
  "current_state": "degraded",
  "mitigation": "traffic_rolled_back_to_model:v1.3.1",
  "next_update": "2027-01-10T14:30:00Z"
}

Checklist for a high-quality postmortem (deliver within 48 hours)
- Timeline: minute-granular actions and who performed them.
- Metrics snapshot: pre/post rollback for error rate, latency P50/P95/P99, request volume.
- Evidence: saved request samples, audit logs, config diffs, canary results.
- Root cause analysis: gap in release gating, test coverage gap, or infra constraint.
- Action items: owners and due dates.

Game day exercise (90-minute module)
Objective: exercise the breachless rollback workflow, measure time-to-mitigate, and validate comms.
Pre-reqs: sandbox cluster, two model variants (stable + candidate), traffic replayer, CS rotation.
Agenda:
1) 00–10m: Briefing and goals.
2) 10–30m: Trigger synthetic regression via deployment that flips a quality flag.
3) 30–60m: Teams execute the runbook: shadow validation, canary, rollback.
4) 60–80m: Communications dry-run using templates and status page automation.
5) 80–90m: Retro and scorecard (time to detect, time to first mitigation, time to restore, customer-communication accuracy).
Scoring targets: detection < 5m, mitigation decision < 15m, restoration < 45m.

Operational hygiene and follow-ups
- Add a pipeline gate: new deploys must run a 15-minute shadow test against a diff-checker for the first 1000 requests.
- Maintain a catalog of stable model variants and their capacity footprints.
- Add automated canary rollback triggers if error rate increases > 3x baseline during canary windows.
- Quarterly tabletop with CS to validate tiering, templates, and SLAs.

Appendix: commands and quick snippets
- Drain worker (example):
curl -X POST https://ops-api.internal/v1/pool/drain -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OP_API' -d '{"pool":"inference-candidate","timeout_seconds":45}'

- Check canary split (example SRE CLI):
# show routing rules
redwoodctl routing get --route inference-text-us-east --format json

- Minimalized status publish script (bash):
#!/usr/bin/env bash
cat <<EOF | curl -s -X POST https://status-api.internal/v1/update -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d @-
{
  "id": "$1",
  "status": "$2",
  "message": "$3"
}
EOF
